definition: Recreational land use is a description of what a particular parcel of land is intended to be used for in the future and in municipal planning. Recreational zoning refers to the laws and regulations that a local municipality or government stipulates to particular plots of land as current open space for leisure, community-use, and outdoor activities. Recreational zoning means the specific area is only zoned for recreational activities. Examples of typical structures and uses allowed within these zones are parks, campgrounds, trails, swimming, and sports facilities. Commercial, industrial, residential structures, or other types of zoning ordinances are not permitted in recreational zones. See: 16 U.S.C. Chapter 1 Subchapter LXVIII—National Conservation Recreational Areas, and Electronic Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR) Title 50—Wildlife and Fisheries Chapter 1, Department of the Interior Subchapter C—The National Wildlife Refuge System, Part 26—Public Entry and Use Subpart C—Public Use and Recreation.
